questions.prompt: A machine takes in 800 J and gives out 600 J of useful work. What is its efficiency (%)?
Explain why a cyclist freewheeling down a hill can reach the bottom going fast, but can never freewheel up a higher hill on the other side.
questions.modelAnswer: At the top the cyclist has gravitational potential energy, which becomes kinetic energy on the way down. Going up the other side, kinetic energy turns back into potential energy. Energy is conserved, and some is always dissipated by friction and air resistance, so there is never enough energy to rise higher than the starting point.
rubric: Energy conserved and some dissipated, so cannot exceed starting height
questions.explain: Criterion D: applying conservation of energy.
